correctness.rationale: PASS. At each degree-three prism vertex, unique plurality of its own color holds exactly when at least two of three neighboring colors agree. If any rung has distinct top and bottom colors, each vertex has an opponent vertical neighbor and needs both horizontal neighbors to agree, propagating uniform differently-colored layers around the cycle. Otherwise all rungs are monochromatic and the cyclic word of rung colors has no singleton monochromatic run. Count constant-rung words plus cyclic r>=2 run partitions with lengths >=2, requiring adjacent run colors distinct; add k(k-1) layer-separated assignments. Formal cycle-run generating logarithms yield L_n(k)=T_n(k)+(k-1)s_n+k(k-1), with T_n=T_{n-1}+(k-1)T_{n-2}, s_n six-periodic, and rational OGF; roots give asymptotic for k>=2. Independent direct plurality enumeration (seven (n,k) cases, including n=3 with repeated cyclic adjacency checked as distinct edges) matches finite polynomial values. That finite test is not an all-n proof.
